title: Fermions and the Tsirelson Problem in Real Quantum Theory
abstract: In a previous work, we showed that real quantum theory (RQT) cannot be experimentally distinguished from ordinary quantum theory (QT). In this paper, we investigate whether this indistinguishability survives two natural extensions of the setting: allowing separated measurements to be represented by commuting rather than tensor-product observables, and imposing superselection rules, as in fermionic information theory. We show that it does in both cases.   Our first result is a positive answer to the Tsirelson problem in RQT: commuting and tensor-product measurements generate the same finite-dimensional correlations. This is surprisingly not a trivial consequence of the standard complex proof, as it does not carry over to the reals. The proof obstruction becomes particularly relevant in the presence of superselection rules, which is why we first establish the equivalence in RQT before extending the framework to superselected RQT.   Our second result is a local, real quantum formulation of superselected theories. We extend the RQT framework to accommodate a representation of superselection over the reals and show, in particular, that it admits a fermionic version whose predictions are experimentally indistinguishable from those of fermionic information theory. More generally, the construction extends to all superselected QTs.
summary: This work rigorously examines how Real Quantum Theory (RQT) behaves when subjected to two physical constraints: using commuting measurements instead of tensor products, or imposing superselection rules. The authors prove that the equivalence between these measurement definitions holds in RQT, solving the Tsirelson problem for real systems, and successfully construct a local, real framework for fermionic theories.
main_problem: The paper investigates the robustness of the indistinguishability between Real Quantum Theory (RQT) and standard Quantum Theory (QT) when extending the framework to include commuting measurements or superselection rules.
main_result: The indistinguishability holds even under these two extensions; specifically, the Tsirelson problem is solved positively in RQT, and a local, real formulation for superselected fermionic theories is provided.
method: The authors use algebraic methods, comparing correlations derived from tensor-product versus commuting observables, and analyzing the structure of algebras under superselection constraints.
model_or_system: The study concerns general quantum theories (QT and RQT) applied to finite-dimensional systems and fermionic systems modeled by the CAR algebra. The analysis compares two types of measurement separation: tensor-product vs. commuting observables.
key_observables: Joint probability distributions $p(a, b|x, y)$, and the structure of observables under superselection rules (e.g., parity invariance).
important_parameters: Finite dimensionality of the system; the presence or absence of superselection rules ($\mathbb{Z}_2$ grading).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to finite-dimensional settings for the Tsirelson problem, and the fermionic analysis focuses on locally even observables.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the Tsirelson problem in RQT, proving equivalence for finite dimensions. It then extends this analysis to incorporate superselection rules, culminating in a detailed, local, real formulation of superselected fermionic theories.
why_interesting: It provides deep structural insights into the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics, particularly how physical constraints like reality (real coefficients) and particle statistics (fermions) affect fundamental concepts like locality and measurement compatibility.
